description: Unchanged original Bot IPC schema tests (bot-schemas.test.ts); zod parsing boundary only, no IPC channel, no persistence, no process or network operation.
isolationRationale: Leaf read all 3 original assertion bodies and the 5-file runtime import closure. bot-schemas.test.ts calls only exported parse functions with inline object literals. bot-schemas.ts parses with zod schemas; drogon-bot-contract.ts contributes one runtime import (isTuiAgent); tui-agent-config.ts builds a static config record from string data at module load and orca-cli-command-name.ts is a pure platform-string function; neither touches filesystem, process, network, credentials or timers. The 4 additional staged files (tui-agent, automations-types, mentu-run-contract, worktree/create-types) are reached only through `import type` chains and are erased by the TypeScript transform; they are staged for provenance of the direct type-only boundary of drogon-bot-contract.ts. Their deeper type-only chains (task-source-context, execution-host, folder-workspace-types, mentu-recipe-contract, workspace-source, lineage-types) are type-only as well and are neither staged nor typechecked. No Electron IPC registration, no main-process wiring and no renderer behavior is reached: passing proves only the pure parsing contract at the schema boundary. ws and tweetnacl are staged solely because the reviewed transport package-runtime helper requires its full pinned closure (ws, tweetnacl, optional zod) to stage zod; the executed suite imports only zod from node_modules, and ws/tweetnacl are never loaded. No actual IPC channel, persistence, scheduler, agent launch or inference operation is exercised. Staging/runner writes only in a fresh canonical fixture under .preflight/parity-baseline. This is not a general sandbox.
runtimeImports: zod 4.5.4 (pinned via transportRuntime tree digest, symlinked from source node_modules)
ws 8.21.3 and tweetnacl 1.0.3 staged only as required by the reviewed transport helper closure; never imported by the suite
relative runtime imports are all within the 5 pinned runtime files
typeOnlyImports: deeper type-only chains of the staged type files are not staged or typechecked
sourceVitestConfigDifferencesFromCapsule: Both configurations use node. Explicit Node24 (v24.19.0, /Users/carlos/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin/node) and original installed Vitest 4.1.11 (pinned source entry) are required and recorded; no dependencies are installed.

Minimal capsule config omits renderer aliases (@renderer, @), the ORCA_FEATURE_WALL_ENABLED define and the happy-dom/host-port setup scripts. This runtime closure uses none of those symbols, aliases, DOM or host-port facilities; no .tsx files are involved.

Root GC/webstorage execArgv (--no-experimental-webstorage, --expose-gc), the Windows maxWorkers override and 60s/30s hook/test timeouts are omitted. The 3 tests are synchronous pure parses with no GC/webstorage assertions, no OS-specific branches and no timed waits; default Vitest timeouts and the runner's outer bound apply. Not full source-environment equivalence.
Source include glob src/**/*.test.ts would run the whole source suite; the capsule executes only the pinned entry test file, as declared.
testEvidenceBoundary: 3 declared cases inspected in src/main/ipc/bot-schemas.test.ts:5-80 (bounded Bot create with harness-default model policy; rejection of unsupported harnesses and undeclared payload fields; responsibility trigger semantics at the IPC boundary). Passing does not prove Electron IPC registration, main-process wiring, renderer behavior or any live bot operation. Preserve exact original test bytes; assertions are not replaced.
